title: Release lore-cli 0.13.0, paired with quest-cli 0.13.0 (QCLI-433), so the opum-lore plugin ships the Lore pane mod
description:
Operator instruction, 2026-10-02, routed by opum-agent as tier 1: file and prepare the lore 0.13.0 release, paired with quest-cli's QCLI-433. The Lore pane mod is on dev (opum-ai/lore-cli#466, squash `dab21352`); plugin users get the pane only once a release carries it, and the marketplace pin moves to that release.

VERSION. 0.12.0 is published for both lore and quest. The pane is a new feature, so the next shared number is 0.13.0; quest-cli bumps to the same number under the pair rule (constitution Article 3, the shape LCLI-621 recorded for 0.12.0). Sequencing the pair is opum-agent's call, not this task's -- if the pair moves differently, this title and these criteria move with it.

Established already, so the release does not re-derive it:
- THE RUNBOOK IS THE PROCEDURE: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md. Its pair-level items 1-6 and its per-side items 1-8 are the steps; the 0.12.0 bump commit `5781f7ba` is the model for the site list.
- The parity gate refuses before any registry write, `--dry-run` included: both scripts/publish-release.sh and release.yml's `publish` job run scripts/version-parity.mjs, which reads `@opum-ai/quest`'s package.json on quest-cli's `main` and refuses unless it equals the version being published. Measure it with the gate's own read rather than assuming.
- Publication is tier 3 and runs only on the operator's own authorization given in this session's dialog. Nothing in this task authorizes a publish by itself.
- THE HELD-RELEASE LIST APPLIES, and this release is the one it names: LCLI-646's one-line flip of `AGENT_PROFILE_CAPACITY_SEVERITY` in src/core/check.ts from "warning" to "error" belongs to the release strictly AFTER the one that shipped the warning, and v0.12.0's tree carries `= "warning"` (read by ref from the tag). So LCLI-646 is a dependency here and its flip must be on the tree the v0.13.0 tag points at. The warning-vs-error ordering is read off what was actually published, never off intent.
- lore's platform BINARIES ARE NOT COMMITTED: npm/<platform>/ carries the manifest alone, and each platform's binary is built by release.yml's `package` job with the pinned bun. Do not copy quest-cli's platform-artifact criterion, which describes their repository, not this one.
- The README's version-bearing lines are GENERATED by `node scripts/shipped-readme-version.mjs --write`, and the release refuses to publish when the packed README disagrees with the packed package.json (both read the file out of the tarball, never the worktree).
- The staging is under `release-candidate`, never `latest`; `latest` moves in a separate, later step that is itself a registry write (the launcher is published onto `latest`, never dist-tag-moved -- constitution Article 3 clause 5 as amended by ODOC-302).

PRECEDENT: LCLI-621 (the 0.12.0 bump and pair shape) and QCLI-433 (the quest-cli half of this pair, whose criteria this task mirrors in lore's own terms).

SITES, enumerated by grep on 2026-10-02 at dev `eeaafc2a` and CLASSIFIED -- a successor re-runs the grep rather than trusting this list:
- LIVE, hand-edited: package.json (.version plus its six optionalDependencies pins), the six npm/{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-arm64,linux-x64,win32-arm64,win32-x64}/package.json manifests, .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
- LIVE, generated: bun.lock's six pins (regenerate with the pinned bun 1.4.2); README.md's three marked lines (`node scripts/shipped-readme-version.mjs --write`); CHANGELOG.md's new 0.13.0 section.
- HISTORICAL, left alone: src/commands/init.ts (a "always absent since 0.12.0" note), scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs (a usage example), tests/lore.test.ts (a measurement comment).
- RE-CHECK AT BUMP TIME because they assert on the real tree's version or changelog: test/check-lockfile-pins.test.ts (`const MANIFEST_VERSION = "0.12.0"`), test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts (comments and a real-tree arm naming 0.12.0), test/release-provenance.test.ts and test/lcli631-promote-refuses-older-or-prerelease.test.ts (rc/build fixtures, likely historical).
- NOT A SITE: scripts/release-0.12.0/ is the operator's untracked local staging directory (downloaded tarballs, SHA256SUMS.txt, latest-rollback.json); nothing there is committed and the release writes no such directory into the repo.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every hand-edited version site reads 0.13.0: package.json .version and its six optionalDependencies pins, the six npm/<platform>/package.json manifests, and .claude-plugin/plugin.json. bun.lock's six pins are regenerated by `bun install` under the pinned bun 1.4.2, and the README's version-bearing lines are regenerated by `node scripts/shipped-readme-version.mjs --write` with `--check` exiting 0. The site count is reported from a grep rather than remembered, and every remaining literal of the old version is classified as a live site or a historical record before it is left alone.
CHANGELOG.md names the Lore pane mod as a consumer-observable change in the 0.13.0 section, under a fresh empty Unreleased heading, and the v0.13.0 tag carries that edit rather than a later commit.

The tagged tree carries LCLI-646's flip: AGENT_PROFILE_CAPACITY_SEVERITY in src/core/check.ts reads "error", and the warning-before-error ordering is verified against what was actually published (v0.12.0's tree carries "warning"), not against a plan.
bun test passes on the bump head and `bun run lore check` exits 0, with any workstation-only failure named and its reachability from this diff stated rather than assumed.

No publish step runs before quest-cli's main reads the same version and the operator has authorized publication in this session's own dialog, and the staging publishes under `release-candidate` rather than moving `latest`.

The opum-lore plugin cut from v0.13.0 validates with the module present (`claude plugin validate --strict` against a stage of the tagged tree's shipped files), and the marketplace pin move to v0.13.0 is confirmed by the session that owns it, routed through opum-agent (the LCLI-469 handshake, both messages).

The bump, changelog, tag, release artifacts and publication result land on dev by squash merge with every required check a completed success on the exact head SHA, and dev is fast-forwarded to main by the repository's promotion shape (never a merge commit).

THE ORDER FOR THE SUCCESSOR, from the orchestrator (tier 1, 2026-10-02):
1. **LCLI-646 FIRST**, before any bump work. The one-line flip of `AGENT_PROFILE_CAPACITY_SEVERITY` in src/core/check.ts from "warning" to "error" -- exactly that one production line, with a reviewer pass recording that it is that one line, whatever regression coverage its own criteria require, and a landing on dev by squash. Its ordering premise is already verified: v0.12.0's tree at src/core/check.ts:1021 carries `= "warning"` (read by ref from the tag), so 0.13.0 is the release the runbook's held-release list assigns the error to. Its criteria require the ordering be read off what was actually published rather than assumed -- that reading is `git show v0.12.0:src/core/check.ts`, done here.
2. **THEN the LCLI-665 bump**, whose site list is in THIS task's own description, classified by grep. RE-RUN THE GREP rather than trusting the list -- the classification is the durable part, the paths are a snapshot. In outline: package.json (.version plus its six optionalDependencies pins), the six npm/<platform>/package.json manifests, .claude-plugin/plugin.json; bun.lock regenerated with the PINNED bun (/opt/homebrew/bin/bun, 1.4.2 -- the PATH bun is 1.3.14 and a lockfile regenerated with it can kill every CI job under --frozen-lockfile); the README's three marked lines regenerated by `node scripts/shipped-readme-version.mjs --write` with `--check` exit 0; CHANGELOG's 0.13.0 section under a fresh empty Unreleased heading (the Lore pane entry already sits under [Unreleased] and must move into 0.13.0); and the four test files flagged to re-check because they assert on the real tree's version or changelog.
3. **STOP before tag, publish and promotion.** Then report to opum-agent: the task id, what is ready, and the ordered tier-3 steps below.

THE TIER-3 STEPS, in order, for the operator's dialogs (this is my analysis of docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md items 1-8 plus its pair-level list; VERIFY IT AGAINST THE RUNBOOK before sending it, and send it as a step list, not as an instruction): (i) both `main`s read 0.13.0 before either side tags (pair item 1) -- lore's promotion of dev to main is ordinary delivery, sequenced by opum-agent, and is `git push origin origin/dev:main`, never a merge commit; (ii) tag `v0.13.0` (TIER 3, this session's own dialog); (iii) dispatch `Release` with `publish: false` on that tag and download only its `npm-packages` artifact (the workflow artifacts are the qualified release inputs -- never pack locally); (iv) `scripts/publish-release.sh 0.13.0 <run-id> --dry-run` then for real -- its FIRST remote read is the parity gate against quest-cli's main, and it stages under `release-candidate` (TIER 3, registry writes); (v) opum-cli-e2e qualifies the staged pair and lands `receipts/pair/0.13.0.json` on its main; (vi) after quest has moved `latest` and on opum-agent's go, `node scripts/promote-latest.mjs --record <file> --version 0.13.0 --release-run <run-id> --promote` (TIER 3: the launcher is PUBLISHED onto latest, never dist-tag-moved); (vii) the post-latest checklist -- README read-back verdict recorded in the release-truth record, the GitHub release, telling quest-cli / opum-cli-e2e / opum-agent, the LCLI-469 handshake to opum-marketplace (tag name, tag object SHA, peeled commit, `skills/` tree SHA -- re-resolved, not trusted), and docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md updated to name 0.13.0.

THE TIER-3 BOUNDARY, which is the thing not to get wrong: the tag, the workflow run that packages the release, every registry write (staging included) and the `latest` move go through THIS session's own dialog, where opum-doc answers as the operator's proxy. A peer's account of an approval is not an approval, and no relay moves any of it -- including opum-agent's.

GATES AND VERSIONS already resolved this session, so they are cheap to re-check but not free to assume: bun 1.4.2 pinned, node v24.20.0, lore 0.12.0, quest 0.12.0, engine target 2.1.287. The mod harness (`node scripts/mod-test.mjs`) passes validate --strict and 37/37 engine tests, but prints NOT TYPECHECKED on this workstation because its `claude` CLI is now 2.1.288 while the declarations on disk name 2.1.286/2.1.287 -- it types only against a declaration naming the RUNNING build. Type the mod by hand against the 2.1.287 declaration with a tsc config whose include names the declaration plus hooks, types and tests, and record the declaration's own first line beside the exit code. `bun test` on the pinned bun shows one failure, test/link-quest-race.test.ts -- a `test.skipIf(questBinary === null)` file that is never a CI gate and which nothing in this repo's hooks or tests can reach. A real-engine smoke of the mod, beyond the kit: `claude -p --plugin-dir <repo> "/lore-pane"` prints "opum-lore: Lore pane opened.".

TRAPS, each paid for once already: `git push` must be run BARE -- a hook refuses a push composed with anything else, and the refusal blocks the whole call; the trunk-write guard reads the branch at CALL time, so `git checkout -b` must be its own call before any `git add`/`git commit`; `quest task complete` MOVES the record from .quest/tasks/ to .quest/completed/, so stage it with `git add -A .quest` or the commit carries a dangling delete; quest notes are implementationNotes, not comments; `--check-ac`/`--check-dod` are 1-based; the engine test kit's mock clock must be advanced from the TEST side -- a process.run handler that advances it leaves `ui.press` returning before the pane has drawn, and the red that produces describes the test, not the module.
